data_description.name: Display name for this climate control instance

advanced.title: Advanced Settings
advanced.description: Adjust temperature precision and optional sensors.

data_description.enable_motion: Use motion sensor for presence-based adjustments
data_description.motion_sensor: Motion sensor to detect room occupancy
data_description.outside_temp_sensor: Outside temperature: sets the adaptive comfort temperature and whether a fan can help
data_description.outside_humidity_sensor: Outside humidity: used to tell whether outdoor air is drier than the room
data_description.adaptation_interval: How often to adapt temperature (5-60 minutes)
data_description.manual_cooldown_minutes: How long to wait after you manually change a value before the automation adjusts again (minimum 60)
data_description.sensor_stale_minutes: How old this room's temperature reading may be before control pauses. Sensors that report on change go quiet while a room is stable - battery Zigbee devices can be silent for an hour. Use a short window only for sensors that report continuously (5-240)
data_description.heat_stale_minutes: How old this room's temperature reading may be before a heat command is held back until the next report. Cooling and the general limit above are not affected. A value at or above the general limit has no effect (5-240)
data_description.outside_stale_minutes: How old the outdoor reading may be before it is dropped from the comfort model. This is a dead-device window - hours, not minutes - and it judges a sensor that every room pointing at it shares (5-240)
data_description.weather_entity: Weather entity whose hourly forecast night coast reads. Leave empty to run without a forecast: the outside temperature stands in when it is cooler than the room by the dusk outside gap, otherwise night coast does not apply
data_description.pv_power_sensor: Solar PV power sensor (W or kW), used as a sunshine proxy by dusk coast and, with the blind below, by sun load. Leave empty and dusk uses the sun elevation only, and the room has no sun load
data_description.heat_load_blind: Cover on this room's sunny window. With the PV power sensor set, PV at or above the threshold while the sun is up and this blind is not closed counts as sun load: the fan stage is skipped and the room cools at once. Leave empty for no sun load
data_description.heat_load_pv_threshold: PV power at or above which the sun counts as shining on the window, for sun load only (0.1-50, default 1.0)

data_description.motion_hold_minutes: How long the motion sensor must have been off before the room counts as empty and the unit starts later (1-240). Someone walking in while the unit is off gets one evaluation at once. An unreadable sensor counts as occupied

offers.title: Phone Offers
offers.description: Ask on your phone before turning the AC on or off in this room while the room is switched off in Climate Adapt. Off by default.

data.offer_enabled: Offer to turn the AC on or off
data.offer_person: Person or device tracker (offers are sent only while home)
data.offer_suppress_entity: Also stay quiet while this entity is on (optional)

data_description.offer_enabled: Sends a Yes/No notification when this switched-off room would benefit from the AC, and again when it no longer does after you said Yes. Does nothing until a person and a notify service are set.
data_description.offer_person: Offers are sent only while this entity is home.
data_description.offer_quiet_start: From this local time no offer is sent to your phone. Default 23:00. The window may cross midnight; start equal to end means no quiet hours.
data_description.offer_quiet_end: Offers can be sent again from this local time. Default 08:00.
data_description.offer_suppress_entity: For example a bedroom or sleep-mode switch. While it is on, no offer is sent. Leave empty to use the quiet hours only. If it is unavailable or unknown it counts as off. An offer that is held back is not sent later on its own; the next check after the quiet period offers again if the room still needs it.

stale_input.title: Climate Adapt: {name} is not controlling the AC
stale_input.description: `{sensor}` has not reported usable data for {age} minutes (reason: {reason}, threshold: {stale_minutes} minutes), so Climate Adapt has stopped making decisions for **{climate_entity}**. The room is uncontrolled until the sensor reports again. Check the sensor's device (a sensor that stopped transmitting can still look populated in Home Assistant when a retained MQTT payload is replayed at startup). This issue clears itself when fresh data returns.

frozen_input.title: Climate Adapt: {name} is not controlling the AC
frozen_input.description: `{sensor}` has read **{value}** for {age} minutes without a single different value, even though it may still look alive (a sensor that has lost its radio link can keep flickering through unavailable and unknown and come back with the same number). A healthy room sensor never holds one reading this long, so Climate Adapt has stopped making decisions for **{climate_entity}** after {frozen_hours} hours and sends it no new command. The room is uncontrolled until the sensor reports a different value. Check the sensor's device (battery, link quality, re-pair). This issue clears itself when a different value arrives.

stale_outside_input.title: Climate Adapt: {name} has lost its outdoor reading
stale_outside_input.description:
`{sensor}` has not reported usable data for {age} minutes (reason: {reason}, last value: {value}, threshold: {stale_minutes} minutes), so Climate Adapt has dropped the outdoor reading from its decisions for **{climate_entity}**.

The room is **still being controlled** - this is not the same as a stale room sensor, which stops the loop. What is lost is the outdoor input: the comfort temperature falls back to the daily means already collected, and the fan option is unavailable. The comfort floor on cooling is unaffected: it reads the room only.

A reading is dropped rather than held because a frozen value drifts further from the real weather every hour. Check the sensor's device - a battery device that stopped transmitting can still look populated in Home Assistant. This issue clears itself when fresh data returns.

implausible_outside_input.title: Climate Adapt: {name}'s outdoor reading is not believable
implausible_outside_input.description:
`{sensor}` is reporting **{value}**, which Climate Adapt has rejected as impossible rather than merely old ({detail}), so it has dropped the outdoor reading from its decisions for **{climate_entity}**.

**This is not a stale sensor.** The device is transmitting, and recently - the reading was rejected on its *value*, not its age. Replacing the battery or re-pairing will not change it; the device itself is reporting something it cannot have measured. The known signature is an exact 0.0 C arriving together with an exact 0% relative humidity, which is a device saying "nothing" rather than a measurement, because 0% outdoor humidity is not physically attainable.

The room is **still being controlled** - this is not the same as a stale room sensor, which stops the loop. What is lost is the outdoor input: the comfort temperature falls back to the daily means already collected, and the fan option is unavailable. The comfort floor on cooling is unaffected, because it reads the room only.

This issue clears itself as soon as the device reports a believable value again - no restart or reload is needed.
